newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 23.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Washington suggests a military hot line be set up on the Korean peninsual and exchange observers to monitor military exercises in the North and South as part of confidence-building measures, former U.S. senator Sam Nunn says.
- Creditor banks on Tuesday decided to provide 160 billion won in emergency loans to the troubled Kia Group.
- Corporations will be able to double commerical loans to purchase Korean-made facilities.
- Stocks closed sharly lower on Tuesday, pressured by rumours of financial troubles at the Ssangyong Group. The composite index lost 14.95 points to close at 725.98.
- Ruling New Korea Party presidential candidate Lee Hoi-chang on Tuesday suggested that the constitution could not be amended to allow a president to be reelected for a second successive term.
- Jinro Ltd faces failure following the expiration of a pact with creditor banks aimed at protecting it from insolvency.
- Lee Hoi-chang, presidential candidate of the ruling New Korea Party, discussed with President Kim Young-sam ways to reshape the party in preparation for presidential elections in December.
- North Korea has repeated a call for massive food aid and eased U.S. economic sanctions before holding four-party peace talks, a Foreign Ministry official said.
